A worker in Nepal filmed the moment he escaped deadly flash floods that have left hundreds of people dead.

Today, even the statue of Gautam Buddha was swept away by the devastating floods. A symbol of peace, compassion, and hope carried away by the force of nature. 💔🌊 This is not just a statue being washed away. It feels like a reminder of how powerless we can be when nature turns against us. Homes, roads, dreams, and now even symbols that have stood for peace for generations are being taken by the floodwaters, Nepal is hurting today. Behind every flood video is a family praying for safety, someone searching for their loved ones, and countless people watching everything they built disappear before their eyes. 🇳🇵 Nepal–Tibet Border Avalanche & Flood | 26 August 2026 A major ice–rock avalanche near the Nepal–Tibet border triggered a cascading hazard: a large glacier mass collapsed from high elevation, sending ice, rock and sediment into the Lhende Khola. The debris blocked the river and formed a temporary barrier lake, which then released a powerful downstream surge of muddy water, debris and boulders. 🌡️ Possible factors: glacier instability, melting ice, steep crevassed terrain, meltwater lubrication and possible seismic triggering. ⚠️ Some claims remain unconfirmed, so the exact trigger requires scientific investigation. 🌊 Avalanche → Debris Flow → River Blockage → Dam Breach → Flood #Nepal #NepalFlood #NepalLandslide #NepalAvalanche #NepalTibetBorder Himalayas HimalayanAvalanche Landslide GlacierCollapse GlacialLake BarrierLake FlashFlood DebrisFlow LhendeKhola Bhotekoshi ClimateChange GlacierMelt NaturalDisaster DisasterScience EarthScience 26August2026

➡️ DESLIZAMENTO NO NEPAL  Um deslizamento de grandes proporções atingiu #Manang, no #Nepal, neste domingo (27). Uma encosta íngreme desabou perto de áreas residenciais, espalhando uma grande nuvem de poeira e detritos enquanto moradores corriam por campos para deixar a região. Segundo relatos, o deslizamento aconteceu em poucos segundos e deu a impressão de que uma parte inteira da montanha estava desabando. O episódio ocorre em meio a um período de fortes chuvas no Nepal, que vêm provocando inundações e outros deslizamentos. De acordo com as informações divulgadas, ao menos 21 pessoas morreram em ocorrências relacionadas às condições climáticas no país. A new catastrophe has hit Nepal mere weeks after a deadly flood which killed over a thousand people… this time claiming an entire mountain. Dramatic footage has emerged of the moment the mountainside collapsed along the Kali Gandaki River, with a large section breaking apart and sliding directly into the river. The incident comes just one month after the 26th August glacier-and-rock collapse in the Langatang region which triggered apocalyptic flooding, claiming the lives of more than 3,000 people and left thousands more missing. While happening in very close proximity to that disaster, this latest incident cannot automatically be described as having been caused by it. Scientists have, however, warned that warming temperatures, glacier retreat and thawing mountain permafrost are making the Himalayan slopes increasingly unstable.

Nepal’s youngest prime minister Balendra Shah told world leaders at the UN that Nepal’s latest flash floods that killed more than 1,400 people are a “close warning for humanity,” and that action is needed now. On Aug. 26, deadly flash floods caused by a glacial collapse struck Nepal, sweeping through villages along the Nepal-Tibet border, killing more than 1,494 people and leaving more than 6,150 people missing. On Thursday, Sept. 24, Shah addressed the UN General Assembly (UNGA) in New York City for the first time. “The Bhotekoshi-Trishuli disaster was not just a local tragedy; it was a warning to the world. And I ask you today: have we really heard that warning?” Shah said. Shah recalled that UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned of an impending climate disaster at the foot of Mount Everest nearly three years ago, and called out world leaders for failing to act despite local communities and scientists reporting the effects of climate change He said climate change, as seen in the floods, affected people across Nepal and Tibet and will affect everyone. “Climate change does not recognize borders. Glaciers and floods do not travel with stamps on passports,” he said. Shah said that Nepal did not create the climate crisis, contributing less than 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions, but is still paying a “colossal price.” According to Shah, Nepal would need to use 10% of its gross domestic product (GDP) to rebuild from the floods, adding that it cannot be constantly rebuilding. While Shah did not ask for financial aid, he told leaders that the Loss and Damage Fund, the Global Environment Facility and other financial mechanisms remain “grossly inadequate.” “Climate finance must not become another bureaucratic mess through which vulnerable countries spend years that they need help,” he said. “When the house is burning, we do not ask the family to complete 50 forms. We act.” Shah also called for cooperation between Nepal, India and China to improve climate resilience and disaster response across the Himalayas. #nepal #balendrashah #un #climate #fyp
